title: Rest is part of the work
description: Rest is not a reward you earn after the work. It is one of the ingredients the work is made from.

body.heading: Tired minds make expensive mistakes
paragraphs: Anyone who has reread their own exhausted writing knows the pattern: the last tired hour often creates errors that the next morning has to fix. Pushing through can feel productive while quietly costing more than it saves.
Rest is when a lot of invisible work happens. Ideas settle, skills consolidate, and problems that looked solid at midnight often have a visible crack by morning.

body.heading: Plan rest like you plan work
paragraphs: Put breaks in the plan rather than taking them as leftovers: a pause between tasks, an evening off each week, a real stopping time most days. Planned rest does not need to be justified or earned.
Notice what actually restores you. Scrolling often leaves people more tired, while a walk, a nap, music or unhurried company tends to return something. Choose the rest that rests you.

takeaway: Schedule rest as an ingredient of the work, not a prize at the end of it.
